definition: Jaccard between exact accepted plant-ID×WGSRPD3 resource cell sets of two butterfly species, not overlap of their potential geographic envelopes alone

deduced_lower_bound.logic: Within the same 986 host-sharing butterfly pairs, at least |A|+|B|-|U| = 920+366-986 = 300 belong to both A (any new shared-host×region cell) and B (declining exact-host×region Jaccard). This is a rigorous intersection bound, not an individually identified cross-tab.

limits: Potential resources computed from recorded host links and plant distributions, not local realized resource use.
Normalized Jaccard can decrease as total host×region resources increase. This fact cannot identify competition, abundance, host preference or colonization.
All-butterfly pair means are dominated by 27,455 butterfly pairs without any exact shared host; report the 986 sharing-pair subset.
